takeaway: HiDPU compresses disaggregated-storage address maps into continuity-aware segments, keeping tiny learned metadata and hot hash pilots on the DPU for mostly one-DMA lookup.
background: Disaggregated storage maps a huge logical space to remote physical pages. A DPU can remove host software from the I/O path, but its weak cores and small memory cannot hold or traverse a conventional full page table efficiently.
villain: Multi-level tables waste host memory on sparse addresses and require repeated DPU–host accesses; compact learned indexes mispredict on irregular mappings. Updating a complex offloaded index on the DPU would also consume scarce compute and disrupt concurrent lookups.
approach: HiDPU partitions mappings by address continuity: exact linear segments cover contiguous ranges, LPTHash covers partially continuous ranges, and perfect-hash segments cover random ones. A learned upper index and segment metadata reside on the DPU; entries and pilots stay in host memory, with a grouped Pilot Cache. Host-side insertion buffers trigger versioned local rebuilds and occasional global reconstruction.
impact: The design offers a practical mapping-index split for constrained DPUs, using workload structure rather than a uniform representation. The same hybrid indexing idea may transfer to disaggregated memory or other remote address-translation tasks.

evaluation.overview: Enterprise block traces and Filebench, LevelDB/YCSB, and PostgreSQL/TPC-DS traces measure throughput, latency, memory amplification, component gains, reconstruction, sensitivity, and comparison with LearnedFTL.
evaluation.implemented: A HiDPU prototype on Huawei's Hi1823, including hybrid segmentation, DPU cache, host insertion buffer, and versioned two-level reconstruction.
evaluation.setting: A 96-core Xeon Platinum 8260 server with 512 GB DRAM and a Huawei Hi1823 DPU; default DPU state uses a 23.74 KB internal index and 1 MB Pilot Cache.

results.text: On four enterprise traces, HiDPU reports 1.1–5.5× throughput over the DPU page table and 1.4–6.3× over the learned baseline, keeping latency below 6.47 µs at up to 256 clients.
Application-derived traces show 1.3–4.3× throughput over the page table and 1.3–1.5× over the learned baseline, with HiDPU latency below 5.76 µs.
For a projected 1.35 billion 1 MB pages, HiDPU needs 29 GB host memory and 23 KB DPU index space versus 102 GB for the page-table baseline.

limitations: The prototype uses one Huawei DPU and replayed traces rather than a deployed end-to-end storage service. Memory at petabyte scale is extrapolated by extending a trace. Global reconstruction briefly blocks new queries and is reported under ten minutes for 1.2 PB; index quality depends on address continuity and tunable segmentation parameters.
phd_group_signal: The work explicitly designs for DPU constraints—tiny memory, weak cores, expensive PCIe interactions—and tests both compactness and lookup latency. It is a useful example of tiering data-structure state according to where computation and memory actually reside.

claims.text: HiDPU selects exact linear, locality-preserving perfect-hash, or ordinary perfect-hash indexing per segment according to logical-address continuity.
Only learned models, segment parameters, and cached pilots reside on the DPU; mapping entries remain in host memory, yielding one host access for exact or cache-hit lookups.
